It preserves a Pietà in polychrome terracotta and an Eternal Father in marble of the fifteenth century, the reliquary of San Fortunato, an organ of the seventeenth century and wooden busts; the sacristy has marble furniture and a frescoed ceiling with stories of Saint Benedict.
1eejlpu.46: The baroque of the Josafatti in the heart of the village.
g5233a.188: A square-shaped tower dating back to the 15th century, which until the 18th century was the bell tower of the Farfense church built by the monks in 1430; it collapsed partly in 1755 for the erosion of the Oste stream.
pvlniu.37: The fifteenth-century symbol of the country.
33wglw.398: Rebuilt at the end of the eighteenth century at the behest of Monsignor Ciccolini from the rural church of Santa Maria a Pie' di Monte, it has the facade with two twin towers. It preserves the body of Saint Viviana, translated by permission of Pope Leo XIII, a polychrome stucco, a Virgin with Child, the crypt of St. Pontico and the reliquaries collected by Monsignor Ariodante Ciccolini, who gathered more than 400 of them.
14ooavt.40: The church of relics, with the crypt.
zk80ec.359: Museum of sacred art next to Santa Viviana, with the reliquary of San Fortunato attributed to Pietro Paolo de Aurificis (1509) and a 17th-century statue of St. Peter the Apostle; the contacts are those of the Sistine Museums network of Piceno. In summer 2025 was open from 24 June to 17 September, every day from 17:30 to 19:30; access only with stairs.
6f0m2.47: The Renaissance reliquary of San Fortunato.
dw1r7j.246: Oratory of the 11th century used by the Farfensian monks, alternating prayer and work next to their agricultural courtyards: rectangular plan with round apse facing east, frescoes of the 15th century and an Annunciation on the apse.
41ok72.37: A farfense oratory a thousand years later.
1572bc2.342: In a clearing at the foot of Mount Ascensione, built by the monks of Farfa on the ruins of a pagan temple dedicated to Artemis; restored in the eighteenth century, it is dedicated to the Madonna of the Consolation, celebrated on 15 August. It has a nave, terracotta floor and travertine altar; in the garden an oak tree over 23 meters high.
shys3a.49: The monumental oak under Mount Ascension.
17nehss.300: In the hamlet remains the ancient fortified fortress; the church of Saint Lucia, documented since 1381 and with Romanesque portal, was damaged by the earthquake of 1943 and reduced in the sixties, and preserves copies of four tables by Pietro Alemanno (the originals are at the Diocesan Museum of Ascoli Piceno).
wd7vmv.42: Rocca and Romanesque portal in one shot.
1uwtmx0.233: In the former Baronial Palace Cornacchia di Poggio Canoso, with rooms dedicated to woods, river environment, agricultural landscape and peasant civilization, dioramas, panels and naturalistic collections, plus a didactic workshop with projection room.
13rfo40.52: The river and the Picena countryside told the kids.
w5i8l8.192: It preserves a gothic reliquary made of 15th-century embossed copper and a canvas attributed to the De Magistris school with the Madonna del Rosario and costume characters of the Gabrielli family.
1e5u2yy.38: A Gothic reliquary in a fraction.
1gy4hs.185: Church designed by the architect Pilotti of Ascoli Piceno, with in the apse a mosaic of Gaudenzi, of the Vatican school, which depicts the Paschal Christ between Saints and Blesseds of Piceno.
